articles.title: Hopwood Hall College celebrates topping out of new Clegg Building
articles.excerpt: A topping out ceremony at Hopwood Hall College marks a significant step in the construction of the new Clegg Building, set to enhance educational facilities in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
A topping out ceremony was held at Hopwood Hall College on October 26, 2026, marking a significant milestone in the construction of the new Clegg Building. This event celebrated the completion of the building's structure, which is being developed by Willmott Dixon and funded by the Department for Education, Rochdale Council, and the college itself.

The ceremony was attended by notable figures including Principal and CEO Julia Heap OBE, Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, and the Mayor and Mayoress of Rochdale, Faisal Rana and Iram Faisal.

Family members of the late Robert Clegg OBE, after whom the building is named, were also present, highlighting the personal connection to the college. Robert Clegg served as Chair of the Corporation from 2007 to 2018 and made significant contributions during his tenure.

During the event, attendees were taken to the roof of the new building, which offers panoramic views of the borough, including landmarks such as Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Parish Church.

Guests were invited to leave messages on the roof parapet, creating a lasting record of the occasion.

The Clegg Building is expected to provide a modern and inspiring learning environment for students at Hopwood Hall College, enhancing educational opportunities in the area.

As construction progresses, the college community looks forward to the completion of this landmark development, which aims to foster a better learning experience for current and future students.

evidence_sources.captured_text: New college building reaches construction milestone - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS New college building reaches construction milestone A special topping out ceremony marked a major milestone in the construction of the Clegg Building at Hopwood Hall College. Being built by Willmott Dixon and funded by the Department for Education, Rochdale Council and the college, the landmark development is poised to become a modern and inspiring learning environment in the heart of Rochdale. The building was visited by Principal and CEO Julia Heap OBE, Rochdale Member of Parliament Paul Waugh, the Mayor and Mayoress of Rochdale, Faisal Rana and Iram Faisal, among others. Members of the family of the late Robert Clegg OBE, in whose honour the new building has been named, joined as special guests for the event. Robert served as Chair of the Corporation at Hopwood Hall College from 2007 to 2018, making a significant contribution to the college during his time in the role. He passed away in September, 2021. Robert’s wife Anne, son Richard and daughter Emma attended the ceremony to mark the occasion, with Emma continuing the family’s connection to the college as a current part-time adult learner. During the ceremony, the team from Willmott Dixon led visitors to the roof of the structure, which offers sweeping views of the borough, including Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Parish Church. There was then an opportunity for visitors to leave a message on part of the roof parapet in what will now become a permanent record of the occasion. The Clegg Building will allow students of all ages to begin mastering future skills when it opens in late 2027. The development is already inspiring current and prospective learners, with school leavers getting an exciting glimpse of the new facility during the college’s Open Events. READ MORE: Nursery loses bid to keep ‘outbuilding’ caravan Mrs Heap said: “This is a very exciting milestone – not just for the college but also the communities we serve. “The Clegg Building is quickly taking shape and when it opens will allow local people for generations to come to develop the technical skills needed to succeed in their chosen industries. “This investment represents our commitment to ensuring learners have the very best environment in which to achieve their ambitions and we’re so proud to name it after someone who contributed so much to both our college community and Rochdale as a whole.” Mr Waugh said: “It’s fantastic to see Hopwood Hall’s newest Rochdale site becoming a reality. “Thanks to a multi-million-pound investment from the Government, as well as funds from the council and college itself, we will have yet another further and higher education site to make our town proud. “Local youngsters who want a career in tech or creative industries, in catering or art and design, will from next October have a state-of-the-art facility to combine with Hopwood’s high quality teaching.” Mike Walmsley, Director Designate at Willmott Dixon, said: “We’re really pleased to celebrate such a key milestone alongside our valued project partners, as we continue to make great progress on delivering a new cutting-edge sustainable facility for the college. “Hopwood Hall College students have been at the heart of this project. So far our team and local supply chain partners have supported the college’s T Level students through placements and employer-led projects, and have supported a Hopwood Hall College student to gain an apprenticeship with our supply chain partner Keith Walton Brickwork. “We’re looking forward to working alongside the college and its students as we move forward with this important project.” Emma Lambert, Robert Clegg’s daughter, said: “It was just wonderful to see the building and be part of such a special milestone. “We are beyond grateful to the college for helping keep my dad’s name and legacy alive in this way. It really is the most beautiful tribute and he would have been so proud – as, of course, are we.” SUPPORT THE ROCHDALE TIMES: FOLLOW US ON FACEBOOK Got a story? We’d love to hear it! articles.title: Rochdale Council moves forward with Hopwood Hall redevelopment after High Court ruling
articles.excerpt: Following a High Court ruling, Rochdale Council has confirmed plans to redevelop Hopwood Hall, with an emphasis on community use, after ending an exclusivity agreement with Hopwood DePree.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has announced its commitment to the redevelopment of Hopwood Hall following a recent High Court ruling that upheld the council's decision to terminate an exclusivity agreement with American filmmaker Hopwood DePree. The ruling, delivered at Manchester Civil Justice Centre, concluded that the council acted lawfully when it ended the agreement, which had been in place since 2017.

The council leader, Neil Emmott, addressed the future of the historic building during a town hall meeting on October 15, stating that the council is focused on bringing Hopwood Hall back into use for the community.

Emmott expressed openness to DePree's involvement, indicating that if he presents a viable plan, the council would consider it.

However, he noted that the legal process is not yet concluded, as DePree has the option to appeal the decision by November 18, 2026, with a potential extension to November 28, 2026.

The High Court's decision came after DePree claimed he had a legally binding agreement to purchase the hall for £1, based on a planning approval granted in 2022. However, the court found that this approval did not trigger the option to purchase.

The council has already invested over £1.6 million in repairs to the hall, and Emmott assured that any costs awarded to the council, amounting to £114,000, would be reinvested into the project.

As the situation develops, the council remains committed to the restoration and preservation of Hopwood Hall, which is seen as a valuable asset for the local community.

Emmott reiterated that the council's focus is on securing the hall's long-term future, and the outcome of any potential appeal will be crucial in determining the next steps.

articles.title: Court Rules on Ownership Dispute Over Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: A High Court ruling has denied Hopwood DePree's claim to ownership of Hopwood Hall, concluding that Rochdale Council acted fairly in its decision to end the exclusivity agreement.
articles.content_html:
A High Court in Manchester has ruled against Hopwood DePree in his bid to gain ownership of Hopwood Hall, a historic manor house in Rochdale. The ruling concluded that Rochdale Council acted fairly when it ended an exclusivity agreement with DePree, who is a descendant of the family that originally built the hall in the 1420s.

The two-day trial, which concluded on 20 October 2026, centred on DePree's claim that the council had reneged on an agreement allowing him to purchase the Grade II-listed property. The council had previously worked with DePree for seven years to facilitate repairs on the dilapidated site, which is now part of Hopwood Hall College. However, in November 2024, the council stated it would explore other options, citing a lack of a commercially viable business model from DePree.

Following the court's decision, DePree expressed disappointment, stating that the ruling was a significant setback for both his family and the community. He indicated that he and his legal team are considering their options moving forward, while also pledging to monitor the council's efforts to restore the hall for public benefit.

Hopwood Hall has a rich history, having been owned by the Hopwood family until 1922, after which it changed hands several times and fell into disrepair. The council acquired the property in the 1980s and has since been responsible for its maintenance.
